ingredients.item: Whole red snapper, cleaned and butterflied

ingredients.cook_qty: 1/2 onion for the paste and 1/2 onion to serve

instructions: Tear the guajillo chiles open, remove the stems and seeds, and put them in a bowl. Cover with just-boiled water, weigh them down with a plate and leave them for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the fish and pat it dry. Make shallow diagonal cuts about an inch apart in the flesh side, without cutting through the skin. Sprinkle 1 tsp of the salt over the flesh.
Heat a gas grill to medium-high and oil the grates, or set a grill basket over the heat. Use 1 tbsp of the oil.

Drain the chiles. Put them in a blender with half of the onion, the garlic, 1 tbsp oregano leaves, the last 1/4 tsp salt and 1/2 cup water. Blend until smooth, adding water 1 tbsp at a time if it's too thick.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a small saucepan over medium. Pour in the chile paste and simmer for 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's thicker and darker. Take it off the heat.
Spoon 1/3 cup of the paste into a small bowl for the table. Brush the rest generously over the flesh side of the fish.
Lay the fish skin side down on the grill and cook for 3 minutes. Flip it, brush on more paste and cook 3 minutes. Flip again, brush and cook 3 minutes.
Check the thickest part. You're cooking it until it flakes and the paste is dark red with dark edges. If it's not there yet, flip it and cook for 2 minutes.
Brush the last 1 tbsp of oil over the fish and transfer it to a platter.
Slice the other half of the onion thinly and cut the limes into wedges. Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side, then wrap them in a clean towel.
Taste the reserved paste. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve the fish with the warm tortillas, the reserved paste, the sliced onion and the lime wedges.
method_notes: Chef's Pencil, the lead, simmers a paste of guajillo, onion, garlic and fresh oregano until it darkens, coats a butterflied snapper and grills it in a basket with three flips, basting each time. Rick Bayless uses ancho chile with tomato sauce, soy and Worcestershire and serves tacos with onion and lime; Mama Maggie's and A Spicy Perspective use a mayonnaise and mustard marinade. The lead finishes with melted butter, which is brushed oil here for dairy-free. Part of the paste is set aside before the raw fish touches it, to spoon over at the table. Grilled outdoors; no broiler method was tested.
